route: The escape shape as a semialgebraic feasibility set. I wrote E(B,s*) -- the set of parameter vectors of an escape extension of a driven block whose improvement outmap is a prescribed orientation -- as an explicit system, and found that it collapses: (i) the substochasticity of every row makes each layer's drive map (c_L,d_L) substochastic, so "w_L(sigma) lies in an interval" is TWO LINEAR inequalities in (c_L,d_L) (Lemma ec-substochastic); (ii) the sign functional rho of thm:escape-level satisfies the exact identity A' rho(sigma,t) = (f10(t)-t) + Delta (t - f00(t)) for ALL t, which turns the one genuinely semialgebraic bit S into a comparison of two substochastic affine maps; (iii) after that the whole feasibility question over the published block is a finite union of linear programmes, and every one of them is infeasible with an exact Farkas certificate. I then dropped thm:escape-no-beta's hypothesis (the second escape shape, beta's switch action reading alpha with weight A''>0), proved its level theorem, and showed the same two identities kill it too, over the same block, for the same labelling of the outer pair.
object: The feasibility set E(B,s*) of the escape shape, presented not as a semialgebraic set in the seventeen-to-twenty-three raw parameters but as a polyhedron in the FOUR LAYER DRIVE MAPS (c_L,d_L) -- each a substochastic first-passage row over the block's readable coordinates, each acting on the drive line by the fixed-point map Phi_sigma -- linked by the two exact identities A' rho = (f10-t)+Delta(t-f00) and A'' rho = (f11-t)+Delta''(t-f01).
headline: Over the level-two block {c1,c2,c3,c6} driven by y_{c5}, with the outer pair labelled (alpha_2,beta_2), no nondegenerate stopping escape extension -- in the published shape or in the second shape where beta's switch action reads alpha -- has improvement outmap B^2(.^z) for any doubling z in {8,10,24,26}, because a substochastic drive map whose fixed point at sigma=4 lies below 47723619/255897160 is pointwise below one whose fixed point at sigma=0 lies above 1175936917/2026652880 on the whole of [0,10168377/16341335].

results.name: The domination lemma on the level-two drive line
results.statement: Let y_sigma(t) be the values of the level-two block {c1,c2,c3,c6} of prop:b2-realised frozen at the drive t = y_{c5}. Put b = 47723619/255897160, a = 1175936917/2026652880, T = 10168377/16341335. If (c,d) and (c',d') are substochastic (c,c' >= 0, d,d' >= 0, |c|_1+d < 1, |c'|_1+d' < 1) and the fixed points satisfy Phi_4(c,d) < b and Phi_0(c',d') > a, then c.y_sigma(t)+d <= c'.y_sigma(t)+d' for every inner strategy sigma in {0,...,7} and every t in [0,T].
results.why_not_implied: cor:escape-m3 excludes z=8 over this block only under the sign hypothesis R_alpha >= C_alpha, through the concavity of rho; this lemma never mentions R_alpha, C_alpha, A, A' or rho at all -- it is a statement about two arbitrary substochastic first-passage rows and the block's drive line, and it is exactly what the mixed-sign case (which cor:escape-m3 leaves undecided) needs.
results.argument: By lem:ec-substochastic the two hypotheses are the linear inequalities c.y_4(b)+d < b and c'.y_0(a)+d' > a, because t - c.y_sigma(t) - d is strictly increasing (slope of c.y_sigma at most |c|_1 < 1, y'_sigma <= 1). The difference (c-c').y_sigma(t)+(d-d') is affine on each of the 20 refined pieces into which the 13 fences of the drive line and the 6 further switches of the block's Min vertex cut [0,1], so its maximum over [0,T] is attained at 0, at T, or at one of the 11 interior breakpoints below T. For each of the 8 x 13 = 104 pairs (sigma,t) the 14-row system {nonnegativity (10 rows), the two substochasticity rows, the two window rows} together with (c-c').y_sigma(t)+(d-d') > 0 is infeasible, certified by an exact rational lambda >= 0 with lambda^T A = 0, lambda^T b <= 0 and positive weight on a strict row (Motzkin's transposition theorem in its elementary direction: summing gives 0 < lambda^T b <= 0).
results.verification: Exact rational arithmetic throughout, everything recomputed from /data/ssg-proof/scripts/blowup/B2_small_nf.json. The drive line was recomputed independently (14 cells, 13 fences, cell 0 = B^1, cell 8 = B^1(.^e_beta1), matching rem:pinned-escape) together with the finer 20-piece partition on which every y_sigma is affine (asserted by evaluating y_sigma at a third interior point of each piece). 104 Farkas vectors were produced by an exact two-phase simplex written for this route (eclp.py) and re-verified componentwise by an independent script (ec_final.py) that rebuilds the 14 base rows from the normal form and checks lambda >= 0, lambda^T A = 0 exactly in all 10 columns, and the sign of lambda^T b. The base system is feasible (c=c'=0, d=0, d'=(a+1)/2, strict slack 47723619/255897160), so no certificate is vacuous. A first, coarser certificate set over the full 36-row window system (ec_domination_certs.json) was produced and verified first and gives the same conclusion; the minimal set is ec_minimal_certs.json. Files: ec_block.py, ec_cert2.py, ec_minimal_certs.json, ec_final.py.

results.name: No escape extension of the level-two block doubles
results.statement: Let B be the level-two block {c1,c2,c3,c6} of prop:b2-realised driven by y_{c5}, and let the outer pair be labelled (alpha,beta) = (alpha_2,beta_2). For every doubling translation z in {8,10,24,26}, B^2(.^z) is the improvement outmap of no nondegenerate stopping generalised escape extension of B: for every A,A' > 0, every A'' >= 0 (A''=0 being def:escape-ext, A''>0 the second shape), all nonnegative C_alpha, C_beta, R_alpha, R_beta and all nonnegative constants, with NO sign hypothesis on R_alpha - C_alpha.
results.why_not_implied: cor:escape-m3 says exactly: z=24,26 excluded by thm:escape-no-beta, z=10 by an inner reason, z=8 excluded only when R_alpha >= C_alpha, and 'what is not decided is z=8 with R_alpha - C_alpha mixed in sign'. This theorem decides that case, and additionally covers the shape (A''>0) that thm:escape-no-beta does not reach, where z=24 is alive again.
results.argument: Write Z = {0,2,4,5,6}, O = {1,3,7}. The inner clause of thm:ec-level2 confines each drive w_L(sigma) to the set of drives at which the block's outmap AT sigma takes the value the target prescribes; its endpoints are the fences at which an incidence of sigma itself ties (excluded by nondegeneracy), while the other fences and t = 0, t = 1 are interior to it (the block has no tied incidence at t = 0 or t = 1). For z=10 and z=26 some such set is empty (at sigma=0 the layer (0,0) demands the block value 3, and sigma=0 presents only 0,1,5,7), so both die. For z=8 and z=24 the order relations prune the upper component at sigma=3,7 and leave one LOW window (block presents B^1 at sigma) and one HIGH window (presents B^1(.^e_beta1)) per sigma, with sup LOW_sigma <= inf HIGH_sigma, sup LOW_sigma <= T, sup LOW_4 = b, inf HIGH_0 = a. z=8: the drives w00,w01,w11 lie in LOW and w10 in HIGH; at sigma in O put p = w01(sigma); the target forces p < w00 < w10 (so f10(p) > p, f00(p) > p) and rho(sigma,p) < 0 -- for A''>0 because A'' rho(sigma,p) = f11(p) - p < 0 (w11 < p), for A''=0 because w11 = w01 and the target's bit S is 0. The first identity then gives Delta (f00(p)-p) > f10(p)-p > 0, and Delta = 1-AA' < 1 forces f00(p) > f10(p). But Phi_4(c00,d00) < b, Phi_0(c10,d10) > a and p in [0,T], so lem:ec-domination gives f00(p) <= f10(p): contradiction. z=24: for A''=0 the target needs w01 = w11, impossible since one lies in LOW and the other in HIGH (thm:escape-no-beta again); for A''>0 the drives w00,w10,w01 lie in LOW and w11 in HIGH, and at sigma in O with p = w00(sigma) the order w10 < p < w01 < w11 gives A' rho(sigma,p) = f10(p)-p < 0, whence the second identity yields Delta''(f01(p)-p) > f11(p)-p > 0 and Delta'' < 1 forces f01(p) > f11(p), contradicting lem:ec-domination applied to the pair (c01,d01), (c11,d11).
results.verification: Exact rational arithmetic; ec_final.py runs the whole chain and prints OK on every line. Specifically: the 14 cells / 20 refined pieces recomputed from the normal form; no tied incidence at t=0 or t=1; the LOW and HIGH windows recomputed independently in two ways (from the cell decomposition and from the per-sigma segment decomposition) and shown to agree; sup LOW_4 = 47723619/255897160 and inf HIGH_0 = 1175936917/2026652880; every LOW window inside [0,T]; the tournament/inner-window verdicts for all four z in both shapes (z=10 and z=26 lose 19 of 32 drives to empty windows in the second shape, 14 and 15 of 24 in the first); the 104 minimal Farkas certificates re-verified; and the two identities of thm:ec-identity checked exactly at all 21 breakpoints of the drive line and all 8 inner strategies on the published 138-vertex game and on both second-shape games built here. Independent cross-check of the pipeline: run at z=0 it reproduces the published realisation -- all 24 drives of the 138-vertex game of prop:b2-realised fall inside the z=0 windows (the drive w10(4) = 0 exactly, which is why the windows had to be taken closed at t=0), and dl_escape.py's assembly of B^2 from three drives was reproduced. A relaxation-first computation (150 LP branches over the choice of the maximising breakpoint per sigma in O) gave the same infeasibility before the argument was compressed to the domination lemma. Files: ec_verify.py, ec_final.py, ec_win3.py, ec_relax2.py.

results.name: The level theorem for the second escape shape
results.statement: Let G be a nondegenerate stopping generalised escape extension of a driven block: alpha: (0) A y_beta + C_alpha.y + q_A, (1) R_alpha.y + q'_A; beta: (0) A' y_alpha + C_beta.y + q_B, (1) A'' y_alpha + R_beta.y + q'_B with A,A'>0, A''>=0, all readouts nonnegative, every row substochastic with a strict leak, no block row reading alpha. Put Delta = 1-AA', Delta'' = 1-AA''; c00 = (A'C_a+C_b)/Delta, d00 = (A'q_A+q_B)/Delta; c10 = A'R_a+C_b, d10 = A'q'_A+q_B; c01 = (A''C_a+R_b)/Delta'', d01 = (A''q_A+q'_B)/Delta''; c11 = A''R_a+R_b, d11 = A''q'_A+q'_B; and w_L(sigma) = Phi_sigma(c_L,d_L). Then all four (c_L,d_L) are substochastic, the drive on the layer L is w_L(sigma), the inner part of the outmap at (sigma,L) is s_B(w_L(sigma))(sigma), and the EIGHT outer bits are the four edge comparisons of the four drives: O_alpha(0,0) = [w00<w10], O_alpha(0,1) = [w01<w11], O_beta(0,0) = [w00<w01], O_beta(1,0) = [w10<w11], the other four being their complements. So at every inner strategy the outer square is the orientation of the 2-cube induced by the four numbers w_L(sigma), every edge pointing at the larger: acyclic, with sink at the largest drive and source at the smallest. thm:escape-level is the case A''=0, where w01 = w11 and the two alpha-bits on the layers (0,1),(1,1) become its bit S.
results.why_not_implied: thm:escape-level assumes beta's action 1 reads only the block, so it has three drives, w01 = w11, and one bit (S) that is not a drive comparison but the sign of the functional rho; with A''>0 there are four distinct drives, the level equation at (0,1) acquires the factor 1/(1-AA''), and S becomes the comparison w01 vs w11 -- a statement thm:escape-level cannot express, and precisely the escape rem:pinned-escape names.
results.argument: Freezing the outer pair at a layer leaves a system in (y_alpha,y_beta) whose block input is y_sigma(y_beta), no block row reading alpha (lem:readout); eliminating y_alpha gives the four displayed fixed-point equations, and lem:readout gives the inner clause. Substochasticity: |A'C_a+C_b|_1 + A'q_A+q_B < A'(1-A)+(1-A') = Delta, and the three analogous computations. For the outer bits, introduce the four layer maps g_L (each nondecreasing with slope < 1 and fixed point w_L) and observe that at each layer the OTHER action of alpha (resp. beta) is worth exactly g_{L'}(w_L) for the layer L' reached by flipping that coordinate: e.g. at (0,0), beta's action 1 is worth A''y_alpha + R_beta y + q'_B = g_{01}(w00), so beta is switchable there iff g_{01}(w00) > w00, i.e. iff w00 < w01; for alpha at (0,1), multiply the comparison R_alpha y + q'_A > A w01 + C_alpha y + q_A by A'' > 0 and add R_beta y + q'_B to get g_{11}(w01) > g_{01}(w01) = w01, i.e. w01 < w11. The remaining six bits are the same computation.
results.verification: Verified FROM TWO EXPLICIT GAMES built by the Knuth-Yao gadget construction of lem:dyadic-row over the level-two block: EC_SHAPE2_GAME.json (138 vertices: 5 Max, 1 Min, 130 average, 2 sinks; A=502/512, A'=509/512, A''=32/512, C_a=C_b=0) and EC_SHAPE2B_GAME.json (149 vertices: 5 Max, 1 Min, 141 average; A=300/512, A'=260/512, A''=96/512, all four readout vectors and all four constants nonzero). In both, the game is stopping by the trap characterisation lem:trapchar, all 64 profile values were computed by exact rational elimination (cross-checked against mycore.profile_value on two profiles), val_sigma taken as the componentwise MINIMUM over ALL positional tau, no incidence is tied, and the 32-entry improvement outmap read off the game equals the level theorem's prediction exactly; both outmaps are acyclic unique sink orientations (heights 9 and 8). At the level of the normal form the prediction was further checked against direct exact evaluation on 60 randomly generated nondegenerate second-shape extensions of the level-two block (all matched). The two identities A' rho = (f10-t)+Delta(t-f00) and A'' rho = (f11-t)+Delta''(t-f01) were checked exactly at all 21 breakpoints and all 8 inner strategies on both games. Control: the paper's own B2_small_GAME.json was re-verified from the game (138 vertices, outmap = B^2, nondegenerate, USO, acyclic, BA height 10). Files: ec_shape2.py, ec_build2.py, ec_build3.py, ec_shape2_test.py, ec_ident2.py.

results.name: thm:escape-no-beta is sharp: the second shape revives the beta-doublings
results.statement: The hypothesis of thm:escape-no-beta that beta's action 1 read only the block and constants cannot be dropped. For A'' > 0 the drives w01 and w11 are distinct and the three pairwise comparisons (P,Q,R) are replaced by the four edge comparisons of thm:ec-level2; for each of the four doubling translations z in {8,10,24,26} of B^2 and each of the eight inner strategies the demanded eight outer bits are then the edge comparisons of a genuine total order of the four drives -- for z=8, w00<w01<w11<w10 where the readout is even and w11<w01<w00<w10 where it is odd; for z=24, w01<w00<w10<w11 and w10<w00<w01<w11 -- so none of the four is excluded by the tournament. Over the level-two block the inner condition then kills z=10 and z=26 (19 of the 32 drives get an empty window) and leaves z=8 and z=24, which thm:ec-main kills instead.
results.why_not_implied: thm:escape-no-beta proves an exclusion under a hypothesis; this proves that the hypothesis is doing real work, by exhibiting, for each of the four translations and each inner strategy, the total order of four drives whose edge comparisons are the demanded outer bits. Its proof turns entirely on w01 = w11, which is exactly what fails when A'' > 0, so nothing about the A''>0 case follows from it.
results.argument: By thm:ec-level2 the eight outer bits at a fixed inner strategy are the four edge comparisons of w00, w10, w01, w11, and the antipodal pairs are automatically complementary; the only combinatorial obstruction left is that the four arcs must not form a directed 4-cycle. Reading the outer part of B_phi(s,z')(.^zeta) off the table of thm:blowup at the layer L xor zeta and translating each bit into an arc gives, for each of the four zeta and each parity of the readout, one of the eight displayed acyclic orders. The inner condition is then checked against the block's per-strategy segment decomposition of the drive line.
results.verification: Exact; ec_s2tour.py computes, for each z in {8,10,24,26} and each of the 8 inner strategies, the eight demanded outer bits from the paper's outmap of B^2, verifies the four antipodal complementarities, verifies acyclicity of the induced 2-cube orientation, and lists the drives whose inner window is empty (0 for z=8 and z=24; 19 of 32 for z=10 and z=26). ec_swap.py repeats the whole analysis for the exchanged labelling of the outer pair (drive = alpha_2): there the first shape's tournament fails at all four z, recomputing thm:escape-no-beta's remark, while the second shape's does not. Re-run inside ec_final.py.

results.name: What the doubling asks of a block's drive line
results.statement: Let B be any driven block, sigma_lo, sigma_hi inner strategies and b < a reals such that the target's inner condition confines the layer-(0,0)-type drive's fixed point at sigma_lo below b and the paired high drive's fixed point at sigma_hi above a. Put u = y_{sigma_lo}(b), U = y_{sigma_hi}(a) and M(y) = max{c.y+d : c,d >= 0, |c|_1+d <= 1, c.u+d <= b} = min_{mu>=0} ( max(max_i(y_i - mu u_i), 1-mu, 0) + mu b ), m(y) = min{c.y+d : c,d >= 0, |c|_1+d <= 1, c.U+d >= a} = max_{nu>=0} ( a nu - max(max_i(nu U_i - y_i), nu-1, 0) ). If M(y_sigma(t)) <= m(y_sigma(t)) for every sigma and every t in the low windows, then no generalised escape extension of B realises the corresponding doubling. The criterion mentions only the block's drive line: in the Farkas certificates the multipliers of the nonnegativity and substochasticity rows are universal -- they are the multipliers of these two little linear programmes -- and the only block data entering are b, a, u and U.
results.why_not_implied: thm:escape-mixed(b) needs R_alpha - C_alpha >= 0 componentwise and concludes an up-closedness of {phi-tilde = 0} in the block's pointwise value order; this criterion has no sign hypothesis, says nothing about the value order, and is a pair of two-variable linear programmes in the block's drive-line data alone. On the level-two block thm:escape-mixed(b) is silent (the route's own case) while the criterion holds.
results.argument: By lem:ec-substochastic the two window facts are the linear inequalities c.u+d <= b and c'.U+d' >= a, so M(y) is the largest value the low map can take at y and m(y) the smallest the high map can take; M(y) <= m(y) is exactly the infeasibility of the pair together with c.y+d > c'.y+d'. The displayed closed forms are LP duality for the two three-constraint programmes. The conclusion then follows as in thm:ec-main, since the identities of thm:ec-identity force the low map to exceed the high map at a point of the low windows.
results.verification: ec_crit.py solves both little programmes in exact rational arithmetic at all 8 x 13 = 104 pairs (sigma,t) of the level-two block with sigma_lo = 4, b = 47723619/255897160, sigma_hi = 0, a = 1175936917/2026652880: M <= m everywhere, with least margin m - M = 1204786569985001139227975/123658871785688451847910352 = 0.009743... at sigma = 4, t = 10168377/16341335. The naive two-term relaxation max_i (y_i-u_i)^+ + max_i (U_i-y_i)^+ <= a-b of the same criterion FAILS at 14 of the 104 pairs (worst -0.0721 at sigma=3, t=0), so the pair of linear programmes, not a triangle inequality, is what does the work. Re-run inside ec_final.py.

restatements.label: thm:escape-level
restatements.note: The identity A' rho(sigma,t) = (f10(t)-t) + Delta (t - f00(t)) follows in three lines from the manipulation already inside thm:escape-level's proof ('multiply by A' > 0 and add C_beta y + q_B'), done at a general t instead of at a fixed point; only its use at t = w01(sigma), which is a fixed point of neither map, is new. The companion A'' rho = (f11-t) + Delta''(t-f01) is genuinely new because it needs A'' > 0, and it is reported as part of thm:ec-level2.

restatements.label: thm:escape-level
restatements.note: That the three published drive maps (D-hat, e-hat), (D_1, e_1), (R_beta, q'_B) are substochastic, and hence that 'w_L(sigma) < e' is the linear inequality c_L . y_sigma(e) + d_L < e, is implicit in thm:escape-level's uniqueness clause (|c|_1 < 1, y_sigma nondecreasing with slope at most 1); only the fourth map (A''R_alpha + R_beta, A''q'_A + q'_B) and the sharpened bound |c_L|_1 + d_L < 1 are new.

restatements.label: rem:pinned-escape
restatements.note: The 14 cells and 13 fences of the level-two block's drive line, and the exact fence values, were recomputed here from the normal form and agree with the published list; they are input to this route, not output.

gap: The exchanged labelling of the outer pair in the SECOND shape. Exactly: no nondegenerate stopping generalised escape extension of the level-two block {c1,c2,c3,c6} driven by y_{c5}, with A'' > 0 and its outer pair labelled (alpha,beta) = (beta_2, alpha_2) -- so that the block's drive is the coordinate the target calls alpha_2 -- has improvement outmap B^2(.^8) or B^2(.^24). (For the first shape, A''=0, that labelling is excluded for all four doublings by thm:escape-no-beta, recomputed here; for the second shape z=10 and z=26 still die on the inner condition, but z=8 and z=24 pass both the tournament and the inner condition, with the drive orders w00<w10<w11<w01 / w11<w10<w00<w01 for z=8 and w10<w00<w01<w11 / w01<w00<w10<w11 for z=24. There exactly one of the four drives is confined to the HIGH windows and it is not the one the identities pair with the layer-(0,0) drive, so lem:ec-domination does not bite: evaluating the identities at w11 leaves, for the odd inner strategies, the condition f00(w11) > f10(w11) between two maps BOTH confined to LOW, together with a global Delta in (0,1) with max_{sigma odd} X_sigma/Y_sigma < Delta < min_{sigma even} X_sigma/Y_sigma, X_sigma = w11(sigma) - f10^sigma(w11(sigma)), Y_sigma = w11(sigma) - f00^sigma(w11(sigma)). The order relaxation of that system -- three substochastic maps with fixed points in the LOW windows interleaving as displayed, one in the HIGH windows, the algebraic link dropped -- IS feasible, a witness being the reference map c = (1/6, 1/24, 1/8, 1/24), d = 1/12 in ec_s2_hit_3.json, so a certificate must use the Delta conditions.)
next_steps: 1. Close the gap above: it is the same finite programme, with the two Delta-ratio conditions added and the algebraic link A''(c10 - Delta c00) = A'(c11 - Delta'' c01) imposed; ec_s2param.py already reduces it, for fixed (A,A',A''), to a linear programme in the twenty parameters (C_alpha, C_beta, R_alpha, R_beta, q_A, q'_A, q_B, q'_B), so the remaining work is a branch and bound over three scalars. 2. The criterion prop:ec-criterion is a test any candidate 5-Max block for B^3 must pass, and it costs two small linear programmes per (sigma,t): it should be run on candidate blocks BEFORE any realisation search, in particular on the level-two GAME read as a block driven by a level-three beta (the shape of prop:b3-outer minus its outer pair), where the LOW/HIGH windows come from B^2 and B^2(.^z). 3. The route's real lesson for rem:pinned-escape is that the escape must come from the BLOCK, not from the outer pair: over this block every escape shape, pinned or not, single- or double-reading, is now dead, so a driven block presenting B^2 at one drive and B^2(.^z) at another must have a drive line whose criterion M <= m FAILS somewhere -- that is a design constraint one can search against directly, and it is a much smaller search space than the seventeen parameters of thm:escape-level. 4. thm:ec-level2's observation that the second shape's outer square is potential-induced (every edge points at the larger drive, so the square's sink is the layer of largest drive) is a general fact about two Max vertices reading each other; it may be worth testing whether it survives when the outer pair is a Max and a Min vertex, which would be the first place a Min vertex could break the acyclicity of an outer square.
games_built: TWO NEW GAMES, both built from a harmonic normal form over the level-two block by the Knuth-Yao gadget construction of lem:dyadic-row (denominator 512, sinks carried as sentinels and mapped last), and both verified FROM THE GAME by verify.py's analyse(): stopping by the trap characterisation lem:trapchar (mycore.is_stopping); all 64 profile values by exact rational elimination of the average vertices in reverse topological order, cross-checked against mycore.profile_value on two profiles; val_sigma taken as the componentwise MINIMUM over ALL positional tau and checked to be a fixed point of T_sigma; nondegeneracy (no tied incidence at any of the 32 Max strategies); the 32-entry improvement outmap; USO, acyclicity and bottom-antipodal heights by auso.py. \begin{definition}[The generalised escape extension]\label{def:ec-escape2}
A \emph{generalised escape extension} of a driven block $\mathfrak B$ with drive $\beta$ is the
game on $C\cup\{\alpha,\beta\}$, $\alpha,\beta\in\Vmax$, with
\[
 \alpha:\ (0)\ A\,y_\beta+C_\alpha\!\cdot\!y+q_A,\quad(1)\ R_\alpha\!\cdot\!y+q'_A;
 \qquad
 \beta:\ (0)\ A'y_\alpha+C_\beta\!\cdot\!y+q_B,\quad(1)\ A''y_\alpha+R_\beta\!\cdot\!y+q'_B,
\]
$A,A'>0$, $A''\ge0$, $C_\alpha,C_\beta,R_\alpha,R_\beta\ge0$, every row substochastic with a
strict leak, and no row of $\mathfrak B$ reading $\alpha$. \Cref{def:escape-ext} is the case
$A''=0$; we call $A''>0$ the \emph{second escape shape}. Put $\Delta:=1-AA'$,
$\Delta'':=1-AA''$ and, with $y_\sigma(t)$ the block's values at the drive $t$ and
$\Phi_\sigma(c,d)$ the unique $t\in[0,1]$ with $t=c\cdot y_\sigma(t)+d$,
\[
\begin{array}{llll}
 c_{00}=\dfrac{A'C_\alpha+C_\beta}{\Delta}, & d_{00}=\dfrac{A'q_A+q_B}{\Delta}; &
 c_{10}=A'R_\alpha+C_\beta, & d_{10}=A'q'_A+q_B;\\[2mm]
 c_{01}=\dfrac{A''C_\alpha+R_\beta}{\Delta''}, & d_{01}=\dfrac{A''q_A+q'_B}{\Delta''}; &
 c_{11}=A''R_\alpha+R_\beta, & d_{11}=A''q'_A+q'_B,
\end{array}
\]
$w_L(\sigma):=\Phi_\sigma(c_L,d_L)$ and $f^\sigma_L(t):=c_L\cdot y_\sigma(t)+d_L$.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[The four drive maps are substochastic]\label{lem:ec-substochastic}
In a generalised escape extension $c_L\ge0$, $d_L\ge0$ and $|c_L|_1+d_L<1$ for each of the four
layers $L$. Consequently $t\mapsto f^\sigma_L(t)$ is nondecreasing with slope at most
$|c_L|_1<1$, so $t-f^\sigma_L(t)$ is strictly increasing and, for every $e\in[0,1]$,
\[
 w_L(\sigma)<e\iff f^\sigma_L(e)<e,\qquad w_L(\sigma)>e\iff f^\sigma_L(e)>e .
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Nonnegativity is clear and $\Delta,\Delta''>0$ because $A,A',A''<1$. Substochasticity of the four
rows reads $|C_\alpha|_1+q_A<1-A$, $|R_\alpha|_1+q'_A<1$, $|C_\beta|_1+q_B<1-A'$,
$|R_\beta|_1+q'_B<1-A''$. Hence
$|A'C_\alpha+C_\beta|_1+A'q_A+q_B<A'(1-A)+(1-A')=\Delta$, so $|c_{00}|_1+d_{00}<1$;
$|A'R_\alpha+C_\beta|_1+A'q'_A+q_B<A'+(1-A')=1$;
$|A''C_\alpha+R_\beta|_1+A''q_A+q'_B<A''(1-A)+(1-A'')=\Delta''$; and
$|A''R_\alpha+R_\beta|_1+A''q'_A+q'_B<A''+(1-A'')=1$. The slope bound is that of
\Cref{thm:escape-level} ($y'_\sigma\le\bbone$), and the displayed equivalences follow because a
strictly increasing function is negative exactly below its unique zero.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The level theorem for the second escape shape]\label{thm:ec-level2}
Let $G$ be a nondegenerate stopping generalised escape extension. On the layer
$(\sigma_\alpha,\sigma_\beta)=L$ the drive $y_\beta$ equals $w_L(\sigma)$, and the inner part of
the improvement outmap at $(\sigma,L)$ is $s_{\mathfrak B}(w_L(\sigma))(\sigma)$. The eight
outer bits are the four edge comparisons of the four drives: writing $[\,\cdot\,]$ for the
truth value and listing whether $\alpha$, resp.\ $\beta$, is switchable,
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
 O_\alpha(0,0)=[w_{00}<w_{10}], & O_\alpha(1,0)=1-O_\alpha(0,0),\\
 O_\alpha(0,1)=[w_{01}<w_{11}], & O_\alpha(1,1)=1-O_\alpha(0,1),\\
 O_\beta(0,0)=[w_{00}<w_{01}],  & O_\beta(0,1)=1-O_\beta(0,0),\\
 O_\beta(1,0)=[w_{10}<w_{11}],  & O_\beta(1,1)=1-O_\beta(1,0).
\end{array}
\]
So at every inner strategy the outer square is the orientation of the $2$-cube induced by the
four numbers $w_L(\sigma)$, each edge pointing at the larger: it is acyclic, its sink is the
layer of largest drive and its source the layer of smallest drive. When $A''=0$ one has
$w_{01}=w_{11}$ and the two $\alpha$-bits on the layers $(0,1),(1,1)$ degenerate; they are then
the bit $S$ of \Cref{thm:escape-level}, and the theorem specialises to it.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Freezing the outer pair at a layer leaves a system in $(y_\alpha,y_\beta)$ whose block input is
$y_\sigma(y_\beta)$, no block row reading $\alpha$ (\Cref{lem:readout}); eliminating $y_\alpha$
gives the four fixed-point equations of \Cref{def:ec-escape2}, and \Cref{lem:readout} gives the
inner clause. For the outer bits, define
\[
 g_{00}(t):=AA't+(A'C_\alpha+C_\beta)\cdot y_\sigma(t)+A'q_A+q_B,\quad
 g_{10}(t):=A'\bigl(R_\alpha\cdot y_\sigma(t)+q'_A\bigr)+C_\beta\cdot y_\sigma(t)+q_B,
\]
\[
 g_{01}(t):=AA''t+(A''C_\alpha+R_\beta)\cdot y_\sigma(t)+A''q_A+q'_B,\quad
 g_{11}(t):=A''\bigl(R_\alpha\cdot y_\sigma(t)+q'_A\bigr)+R_\beta\cdot y_\sigma(t)+q'_B,
\]
each nondecreasing with slope $<1$ and with unique fixed point $w_{00},w_{10},w_{01},w_{11}$
respectively. On the layer $(0,0)$, $y_\alpha=Aw_{00}+C_\alpha y+q_A$; $\beta$'s action $1$ is
worth $A''y_\alpha+R_\beta y+q'_B=g_{01}(w_{00})$, so $\beta$ is switchable there iff
$g_{01}(w_{00})>w_{00}$, i.e.\ iff $w_{00}<w_{01}$. On $(0,1)$, $y_\alpha=Aw_{01}+C_\alpha y+q_A$
and $\beta$'s action $0$ is worth $A'y_\alpha+C_\beta y+q_B=g_{00}(w_{01})$, so $\beta$ is
switchable iff $w_{01}<w_{00}$. On $(1,0)$ and $(1,1)$, $y_\alpha=R_\alpha y+q'_A$ and the same
computation with $g_{11}$, $g_{10}$ gives $[w_{10}<w_{11}]$ and $[w_{11}<w_{10}]$. For $\alpha$:
on $(0,0)$ it is switchable iff $R_\alpha y+q'_A>Aw_{00}+C_\alpha y+q_A$; multiplying by $A'>0$
and adding $C_\beta y+q_B$ turns this into $g_{10}(w_{00})>g_{00}(w_{00})=w_{00}$, i.e.\
$w_{00}<w_{10}$; on $(1,0)$ the reverse; on $(0,1)$ multiply the same comparison at the drive
$w_{01}$ by $A''$ and add $R_\beta y+q'_B$ to get $g_{11}(w_{01})>g_{01}(w_{01})=w_{01}$, i.e.\
$w_{01}<w_{11}$; on $(1,1)$ the reverse. (Verified from two explicit games,
\texttt{EC\_SHAPE2\_GAME.json} on $138$ vertices and \texttt{EC\_SHAPE2B\_GAME.json} on $149$,
and on $60$ further random nondegenerate extensions of the level-two block at the level of the
normal form; \texttt{ec\_build2.py}, \texttt{ec\_build3.py}, \texttt{ec\_shape2\_test.py}.)
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[The two escape identities]\label{thm:ec-identity}
Let $\rho(\sigma,t):=(R_\alpha-C_\alpha)\cdot y_\sigma(t)+(q'_A-q_A)-At$ be the functional of
\Cref{thm:escape-level}. In every generalised escape extension, for all $\sigma$ and all
$t\in[0,1]$,
\[
 A'\,\rho(\sigma,t)=\bigl(f^\sigma_{10}(t)-t\bigr)+\Delta\bigl(t-f^\sigma_{00}(t)\bigr),

\]
\end{theorem}

$A'(q'_A-q_A)=d_{10}-\Delta d_{00}$, so

\begin{theorem}[No escape extension of the level-two block doubles]\label{thm:ec-main}
Let $\mathfrak B_2$ be the level-two block of \Cref{prop:b2-realised} driven by $y_{c_5}$, and let
$(\alpha,\beta)=(\alpha_2,\beta_2)$. For every doubling translation $z\in\{8,10,24,26\}$,
$B^{2}(\cdot\oplus z)$ is the improvement outmap of no nondegenerate stopping generalised escape
extension of $\mathfrak B_2$ --- for every $A,A'>0$, every $A''\ge0$, all nonnegative
$C_\alpha,C_\beta,R_\alpha,R_\beta$ and all constants, with no sign hypothesis on
$R_\alpha-C_\alpha$. This closes the case \Cref{cor:escape-m3} leaves open, and it closes it for
the shape \Cref{thm:escape-no-beta} does not reach.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Write $Z:=\{0,2,4,5,6\}$ and $O:=\{1,3,7\}$ for the inner strategies at which the target demands
$\tilde\varphi=0$, resp.\ $1$.

\emph{The windows.} By \Cref{thm:ec-level2} the inner part of the outmap at $(\sigma,L)$ is
$s_{\mathfrak B_2}(w_L(\sigma))(\sigma)$, so $w_L(\sigma)$ is confined to the set of drives at
which the block's outmap at $\sigma$ takes the value the target prescribes. That set is a union
of intervals whose endpoints are the fences at which an incidence \emph{of $\sigma$} ties, which
nondegeneracy excludes; the fences at which some other incidence ties are interior to it, and
$t=0$, $t=1$ belong to it, the block having no tied incidence there. For $z=10$ and $z=26$ some
such set is empty --- at $\sigma=0$ the layer $(0,0)$ demands the value $3$, and $\sigma=0$
presents only $0,1,5,7$ --- so those two are excluded. For $z=8$ and $z=24$ the order relations
of \Cref{cor:ec-no-beta-fails} prune the second component at $\sigma=3,7$ and leave, for every
$\sigma$, one interval $\mathrm{LOW}_\sigma$ (where the block presents $B^{1}$ at $\sigma$) and
one interval $\mathrm{HIGH}_\sigma$ (where it presents $B^{1}(\cdot\oplus e_{\beta_1})$), with
$\sup\mathrm{LOW}_\sigma\le\inf\mathrm{HIGH}_\sigma$,
$\sup\mathrm{LOW}_\sigma\le T$, $\sup\mathrm{LOW}_4=b$ and $\inf\mathrm{HIGH}_0=a$. For $z=8$
the drives $w_{00},w_{01},w_{11}$ are confined to $\mathrm{LOW}$ and $w_{10}$ to
$\mathrm{HIGH}$; for $z=24$, $w_{00},w_{10},w_{01}$ to $\mathrm{LOW}$ and $w_{11}$ to
$\mathrm{HIGH}$. For $z=24$ and $A''=0$ one has $w_{01}=w_{11}$, which is impossible since the
two lie in disjoint intervals --- this is \Cref{thm:escape-no-beta} again --- so $A''>0$ there.

\emph{$z=8$.} Fix $\sigma\in O$ and put $p:=w_{01}(\sigma)$. The target demands
$p<w_{00}(\sigma)<w_{10}(\sigma)$, and $w_{11}(\sigma)<p$ when $A''>0$
(\Cref{cor:ec-no-beta-fails}). By \Cref{lem:ec-substochastic}, $f_{10}(p)>p$ and $f_{00}(p)>p$.
If $A''>0$, the second identity of \Cref{thm:ec-identity} at $t=p$ reads
$A''\rho(\sigma,p)=f_{11}(p)-p<0$; if $A''=0$ then $w_{11}=w_{01}=p$ and the bit $S$ of
\Cref{thm:escape-level} demanded by the target is $0$, i.e.\ again $\rho(\sigma,p)<0$. The first
identity then gives $\bigl(f_{10}(p)-p\bigr)+\Delta\bigl(p-f_{00}(p)\bigr)<0$, i.e.\
$\Delta\bigl(f_{00}(p)-p\bigr)>f_{10}(p)-p>0$; since $\Delta=1-AA'<1$ this forces
$f_{00}(p)>f_{10}(p)$. But $\Phi_4(c_{00},d_{00})\in\mathrm{LOW}_4$ gives
$\Phi_4(c_{00},d_{00})<b$, $\Phi_0(c_{10},d_{10})\in\mathrm{HIGH}_0$ gives
$\Phi_0(c_{10},d_{10})>a$, and $p\in\mathrm{LOW}_\sigma\subseteq[0,T]$, so
\Cref{lem:ec-domination} gives $f_{00}(p)\le f_{10}(p)$ --- a contradiction.

\emph{$z=24$.} Fix $\sigma\in O$ and put $p:=w_{00}(\sigma)$. The order is
$w_{10}<p<w_{01}<w_{11}$, so $f_{10}(p)<p$, $f_{01}(p)>p$, $f_{11}(p)>p$. The first identity at
$t=p$ reads $A'\rho(\sigma,p)=f_{10}(p)-p<0$, so $\rho(\sigma,p)<0$; the second gives
$\bigl(f_{11}(p)-p\bigr)+\Delta''\bigl(p-f_{01}(p)\bigr)<0$, i.e.\
$\Delta''\bigl(f_{01}(p)-p\bigr)>f_{11}(p)-p>0$, and $\Delta''<1$ forces $f_{01}(p)>f_{11}(p)$.

\Cref{lem:ec-domination}, applied to the pair $(c_{01},d_{01})$, $(c_{11},d_{11})$, gives
$f_{01}(p)\le f_{11}(p)$ --- a contradiction.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[What the doubling asks of a block's drive line]\label{prop:ec-criterion}
Let $\mathfrak B$ be any driven block, $\sigma_{\mathrm{lo}},\sigma_{\mathrm{hi}}$ inner
strategies and $b<a$ reals such that the target's inner condition confines the low map's fixed
point at $\sigma_{\mathrm{lo}}$ below $b$ and the high map's fixed point at
$\sigma_{\mathrm{hi}}$ above $a$. Put $u:=y_{\sigma_{\mathrm{lo}}}(b)$,
$U:=y_{\sigma_{\mathrm{hi}}}(a)$ and, for a value vector $y$,
\[
 \mathrm M(y):=\max\{c\cdot y+d:\ c,d\ge0,\ |c|_1+d\le1,\ c\cdot u+d\le b\}
  =\min_{\mu\ge0}\Bigl(\max\bigl(\max_i(y_i-\mu u_i),\,1-\mu,\,0\bigr)+\mu b\Bigr),
\]
\[
 \mathrm m(y):=\min\{c\cdot y+d:\ c,d\ge0,\ |c|_1+d\le1,\ c\cdot U+d\ge a\}
  =\max_{\nu\ge0}\Bigl(a\nu-\max\bigl(\max_i(\nu U_i-y_i),\,\nu-1,\,0\bigr)\Bigr).
\]
If $\mathrm M(y_\sigma(t))\le \mathrm m(y_\sigma(t))$ for every $\sigma$ and every $t$ in the low
windows, then no generalised escape extension of $\mathfrak B$ realises the corresponding
doubling. The condition mentions only the block's drive line: in the Farkas certificates of
\Cref{lem:ec-domination} the multipliers of the nonnegativity and substochasticity rows are
universal --- they are the multipliers of the two little linear programmes above --- and the
only block data entering are the two numbers $b,a$ and the two vectors $u,U$. On
$\mathfrak B_2$, with $\sigma_{\mathrm{lo}}=4$, $\sigma_{\mathrm{hi}}=0$ and $b,a$ as in
\Cref{lem:ec-domination}, the criterion holds with least margin
$\mathrm m-\mathrm M=\tfrac{1204786569985001139227975}{123658871785688451847910352}
 =0.00974\ldots$ at $\sigma=4$, $t=T$; the two-term relaxation
$\max_i(y_i-u_i)^{+}+\max_i(U_i-y_i)^{+}\le a-b$ of the same criterion is \emph{not} enough --- it
fails at $14$ of the $104$ pairs --- so the pair of linear programmes is what does the work.
(\texttt{ec\_crit.py}.)
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}[The scope of \Cref{thm:ec-main}, and what is left]\label{rem:ec-scope}
\Cref{thm:ec-main} fixes the labelling $(\alpha,\beta)=(\alpha_2,\beta_2)$ of
\Cref{cor:escape-m3}: the drive of the block is the coordinate the target calls $\beta_2$. For
the first shape the other labelling --- the drive being the coordinate the target calls
$\alpha_2$ --- is excluded for all four doublings by \Cref{thm:escape-no-beta}; recomputed here,
its tournament fails at every one of the four (\texttt{ec\_swap.py}). For the second shape it is
not: with $A''>0$ and the drive $\alpha_2$, $z=10$ and $z=26$ still die on the inner condition

and the inner condition, with the drive orders
\[
 z=8:\ w_{00}<w_{10}<w_{11}<w_{01}\ (\tilde\varphi=0),\quad w_{11}<w_{10}<w_{00}<w_{01}\
 (\tilde\varphi=1);
\]
\[
 z=24:\ w_{10}<w_{00}<w_{01}<w_{11}\ (\tilde\varphi=0),\quad w_{01}<w_{00}<w_{10}<w_{11}\
 (\tilde\varphi=1),
\]
in which exactly one of the four drives is confined to the $\mathrm{HIGH}$ windows and it is not
the one the identities of \Cref{thm:ec-identity} pair with the layer-$(0,0)$ drive. There
\Cref{lem:ec-domination} does not bite: evaluating the identities at $w_{11}$ leaves, for
$\sigma\in O$, the condition $f_{00}(w_{11})>f_{10}(w_{11})$ between two maps both confined to
$\mathrm{LOW}$, and a global $\Delta\in(0,1)$ with
$\max_{\sigma\in O}X_\sigma/Y_\sigma<\Delta<\min_{\sigma\in Z}X_\sigma/Y_\sigma$,
$X_\sigma:=w_{11}(\sigma)-f^{\sigma}_{10}(w_{11}(\sigma))$,
$Y_\sigma:=w_{11}(\sigma)-f^{\sigma}_{00}(w_{11}(\sigma))$. GAP, exactly:
\emph{no nondegenerate stopping generalised escape extension of the level-two block
$\{c_1,c_2,c_3,c_6\}$ driven by $y_{c_5}$ with $A''>0$, whose outer pair is labelled
$(\alpha,\beta)=(\beta_2,\alpha_2)$, has improvement outmap $B^{2}(\cdot\oplus8)$ or
$B^{2}(\cdot\oplus24)$.} The order relaxation of that system --- three substochastic maps with
fixed points in the $\mathrm{LOW}$ windows interleaving as displayed, one in the $\mathrm{HIGH}$
windows, the algebraic link between them dropped --- \emph{is} feasible
(\texttt{ec\_s2\_hit\_3.json}), so a certificate must use the $\Delta$ conditions.
\end{remark}
